questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Specialized epidermal cells surrounding the guard cells are called:
questions.solution: As subsidiary cells and guard cells both are the modification of epidermal cells in which guard cells have chloroplasts which is absent in surrounding subsidiary cells. Subsidiary cells are the accessory cells to guard cells in the epidermis of plants. Two or four subsidiary cells are found surrounding the pair of guard cells. Subsidiary cells do not consist of chloroplasts. They provide support for the functioning of guard cells in the epidermis. Subsidiary cells play a role in ion channel-mediated opening and closing of guard cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following features is not present in the phylum Arthropoda?
questions.solution: Aquatic annelids like Nereis possess lateral appendages, parapodia, which help in swimming.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which is the National Aquatic Animal of India?
questions.solution: The docile and graceful river dolphin is now India's National Aquatic Animal. The Ganges river dolphin can only live in freshwater and is essentially blind. They hunt by emitting ultrasonic sounds, which bounces off of fish and other prey, enabling them to “see” an image in their mind. They are frequently found alone or in small groups, and generally a mother and calf travel together

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following characteristic features always holds true for the corresponding group of animals?
options: Possess a mouth with an upper and a lower jaw - Chordata
3 – chambered heart with one incompletely divided ventricle - Reptilia
questions.solution:
Reptillia has an order crocodilian which shows 4 chambered heart.

In mammals, prototheria group shows oviparity while metatheria and eutherian show viviparity.

Chordates can be gnathostomata (jawed organism) and agnatha (without jaws).

Only cartilaginous fishes (chondrichthyes) show cartilaginous endoskeleton without any exception.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following characteristics is not shared by birds and mammals?
questions.solution:
Birds are oviparous while mammals are oviparous (prototherians) and viviparous (metatherians and eutherians). Oviparous- producing young by means of eggs which are hatched after they have been laid by the parent, as in birds. Viviparous- bringing forth live young which have developed inside the body of the parent.

The only oviparous mammal is platypus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is wrong for viroids?
options: Their RNA is of high molecular weight
questions.solution: In viroids, RNA is of low molecular weight. Viroids, the smallest known pathogens, are naked, circular, single-stranded RNA molecules that do not encode protein yet replicate autonomously when introduced into host plants. Potato spindle tuber viroid, discovered in 1971, is the prototype; 29 other viroids have since been discovered ranging in length from 120 to 475 nucleotides. Viroids only infect plants; some cause economically important diseases of crop plants, while others appear to be benign.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One of the major components of the cell wall of most fungi is:
questions.solution:
Peptidoglycan - Bacterial cell wall

Cellulose and Hemicellulose - Plant cell wall

Chitin - Fungal cell wall

The chitin adds rigidity and necessary support to the thin cells of fungus and makes the mushrooms fresh.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is wrong?
options: Cyanobacteria are also called blue - green algae
Golden algae are also called desmids
Eubacteria are also called false bacteria
Phycomycetes are also called algal fungi
questions.solution: Eubacteria are the true bacteria, which lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria, chloroplast, etc. Bacteria are cosmopolitan. They can survive almost everywhere, including the bottom of oceans, our month, acidic and alkaline environment, hot springs, puddles, on glaciers, surface water, soil, foodstuffs, petroleum, rubbish, manure, the surface of plants, the surface of animals, body cavities, intestinal tracts of animals, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Chrysophytes, Euglenoids, Dinoflagellates and Slime moulds are included in the kingdom:
questions.solution: Protista is a group created by Haeckel which includes all Eukaryotic unicellular organisms. Kingdom Protista is subdivided into - Protozoa-animal-like single-celled organisms. Protophyta- plant-like single-celled organisms and Slime moulds- fungus-like single-celled organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Mitochondria and chloroplast are:

(i) Semi - autonomous organelles

(ii) Formed by the division of pre-existing organelles and they contain DNA but lack protein synthesizing machinery

Which one of the following option is correct?
questions.solution: Mitochondria and chloroplast are semi-autonomous organelles and they have their own ribosomes with the help of which they can synthesize protein.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Microtubules are the constituents of:
questions.solution: Peroxisomes are a microbody. Chromatin consists of DNA and proteins, and it condenses to form chromosomes. A nucleosome is the basic unit of chromatin. Microtubules are structures present in cilia, flagella, centrioles, and spindle fibres.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The region of chromatin that is stained lightly is
questions.solution: In a typical nucleus, some regions of chromatin are loosely packed (and stains light) and are referred to as euchromatin. The chromatin that is more densely packed and stains dark is called heterochromatin. Euchromatin is said to be transcriptionally active chromatin, whereas heterochromatin is inactive. The centromere is mainly composed of heterochromatin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following cell organelles are enclosed by a single membrane?
questions.solution: Lysosomes are the unit membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus rich in hydrolytic enzymes like hydrolases, lipases, proteases, carbohydrases, and nucleases which are optimally active at the acidic pH. These enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids,, and nucleic acids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Water-soluble pigments found in plant cell vacuoles are:
questions.solution: Anthocyanin is stored in vacuoles. They are a type of flavonoid, a class of compounds with antioxidant effects, Found naturally in a number of foods. anthocyanins are the pigments that give red, purple, and blue produced by plants in and stored in vacuoles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a chloroplast the highest number of protons are found in:
questions.solution: During photophosphorylation process, PS-II helps in the photolysis of water molecules, and the PS-II are located towards the lumen of the thylakoid. The photolysis yields number of protons. For the photolysis of the water several cations and anions are needed, like Magnesium, Manganese and Chloride. Thus, the lumen of thylakoid has a maximum number of protons.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In meiosis, crossing over is initiated at _________.
questions.solution: Pachytene is the third stage of the prophase of meiosis, following zygotene, during which the paired chromosomes shorten and thicken, the two chromatids of each separate and exchange of segments between chromatids occurs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Spindle fibres attach on to:
questions.solution: Kinetochore of chromosomes facilitates the attachment of spindle fibre (chromosomal fibre) and the poles. A chromosome consists of two identical halves, the chromatids which are held together at on point called the centromere. On the sides of the centromere, disc-shaped structure are present known as kinetochores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a characteristic feature during mitosis in somatic cells?
questions.solution:
Synapsis is a pairing of homologous chromosomes which occurs during meiosis (Zygotene sub-stage of Prophase-I) but it is absent in mitosis.

Chromosome pairing refers to the lengthwise alignment of homologous chromosomes at the prophase stage of meiosis. Most sexually reproducing organisms have two sets of chromosomes, out of which one set is inherited from each parent.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A cell at the telophase stage is observed by a student in a plant brought from the field. He tells his teacher that this cell is not like other cells at the telophase stage. There is no formation of the cell plate and thus the cell is containing more chromosomes as compared to other dividing cells. This would result in:
questions.solution: Polyploid cells have a chromosome number that is more than double the haploid number. Polyploidy is common in nature and provides a major mechanism for adaptation and speciation. The cells of these plants do not form cell plate at the end of cell division thus the cells have an extra number of chromosomes as compared to other dividing cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The term ecosystem was coined by:
questions.solution: The term ecosystem was coined by A.G. Tansley in 1935. He defined an ecosystem as 'a particular category of physical systems, consisting of organisms and inorganic components in a relatively stable equilibrium, open and of various sizes and kinds.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is a characteristic feature of cropland ecosystem?
questions.solution: Cropland ecosystem has same type of crop plants so it has the least genetic diversity. Cropland includes areas used for the production of adapted crops for harvest.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the pairs of sedimentary biogeochemical cycles.
I. Hydrogen cycle and water cycle
II. Phosphorus Cycle and sulphur cycle
III. Calcium cycle and magnesium cycle
IV. Carbon cycle and nitrogen cycle
questions.solution:
Biogeochemical cycle is of two types:

Gaseous cycles: Exchange of nutrients occurs in gaseous or vapour form. In this cycle, biogeochemical is non-mineral and the reservoir pool is atmosphere or hydrosphere. E.g., Nitrogen, Carbon, Oxygen, Hydrogen cycle.

Sedimentary cycle: In this cycle, biogeochemical is mineral, reservoir pool is earth’s crust or lithosphere. E.g., sulphur, phosphorous, calcium and magnesium cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following, all three are macronutrients?
questions.solution:
Macronutrients are required in the greater amount which is 1 mg-gram of plant dry weight.

The macronutrients include:

• Carbon (C)

• Hydrogen (H)

• Oxygen (O)

• Nitrogen (N)

• Phosphorus (P)

• Potassium (K)

• Calcium (Ca)

• Magnesium (Mg)

• Sulfur (S)

The first three—carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen—are known as structural elements and are present in the atmosphere and growing environment.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The standard petal of the papilionaceous corolla is also called:
questions.solution:
Papilionaceous corolla.


A single, large, upper petal is known as the banner also vexillum or standard petal of a papilionaceous flower.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a stem modification?
questions.solution: Pitcher of Nepenthes is a modification of the leaf. Nepenthes species usually produce two types of pitchers, known as leaf dimorphism. Appearing near the base of the plant are the large lower traps, which typically sit on the ground. The upper or aerial pitchers are usually smaller, coloured differently, and possess different features from the lower pitchers. These upper pitchers usually form as the plant reaches maturity and the plant grows taller. To keep the plant steady, the upper pitchers often form a loop in the tendril, allowing it to wrap around for nearby support.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cotyledon of maize grain is called:
questions.solution:
In maize grains, the single large shield-shaped cotyledon is called scutellum. The scutellum is believed to contain an as yet unidentified protein transporter that facilitates starch movement from the endosperm to the embryo.

Coleoptile is a sheath-like structure that protects the young shoot tip in monocots.

Coleorhiza is another sheath-like structure that protects the young root tip in monocots.

Plumule is the rudimentary shoot or stem of an embryo plant.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Stems modified into flat green organs performing the functions of leaves are known as:
questions.solution: Stem modified into flat green organs performing the functions of leaves are known as phylloclades whereas phyllode is a modification of petiole. Cladode is a flattened organ arising from the stem of a plant. These often replace the leaves in photosynthetic function, as leaves in such plants are typically reduced to scales. Example: Asparagus, butcher's broom. Scale is a modified thick and fleshy leaf.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The coconut water from tender coconut represents:
questions.solution: The coconut water from tender coconut is free-nuclear endosperm (made up of thousands of nuclei) and the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Proximal end of the filament of stamen is attached to the:
questions.solution:
A proximal end of the filament of the stamen is attached to the thalamus or petal, and the distal end is attached to anther.

The terminal, a part of the pedicel, is named the thalamus or torus or receptacle. It's a condensed axis of the flower from which all floral parts arise. Depending upon the gynoecium's position on the thalamus concerning other parts, flowers are of three kinds – hypogynous, perigynous, and epigynous. In many flowers, the thalamus is condensed, and therefore the internodes aren't seen clearly.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tricarpellary, syncarpous gynoecium is found in flowers of
questions.solution: Liliaceae family is a monocot characterised by tricarpellary, syncarpous gynoecium with superior, trilocular ovary with two ovules in each loculus and placentation axile.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Emerson's enhancement effect and red drop have been instrumental in the discovery of:
options: Photophosphorylation and non - cyclic electron transport
questions.solution: The red drop effect occurs due to decreased functioning of PS-II beyond 680 nm and when both PS-I and PS-II are functioning together there is an enhancement in quantum yield. In PS I the reaction centre chlorophyll a has an absorption peak at 700 nm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A plant in your garden avoids photorespiratory losses, has improved water use efficiency, shows high rates of photosynthesis at high temperatures and has improved efficiency of nitrogen utilization. In which of the following physiological groups would you assign this plant?
questions.solution:
C4 plants have a high rate of photosynthesis at a higher temperature. These plants efficiently uses PEPCo enzyme to assimilate the atmospheric carbon dioxide and convert it into a four-carbon compound. 


In C4 plants, RuBisCO capacity limits net CO2 assimilation rate below 20°C in chilling‐tolerant species, but the control over net CO2 assimilation rate at elevated temperature remains high. Therefore, the ability of C4 plants acclimatization remains high.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The Avena curvature is used for bioassay of:
questions.solution:
Among the plant growth regulators, Auxins are one of the major classes which is considered as growth promoters. Auxins are of mainly two types, natural and artificial. Avena curvature bioassay, first demonstrated by Went in 1928, is done to test the function of IAA, which is a natural auxin. The Avena geo-curvature test is a bioassay for auxin-type growth regulators. 

Triple pea test is bioassay for Ethylene. Dwarf pea test is the bioassay for GA3.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In bryophytes and pteridophytes, transport of male gametes requires:
questions.solution: In bryophytes and pteridophytes, the male gametes are motile and they require water for fertilization. Their flagellated sperm must swim through water to reach the egg. So water is an essential element to complete the life cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct statement:
options: Gymnosperms are both homosporous and heterosporous
The leaves of gymnosperms are not well adapted to extremes of climate
questions.solution:
Sequoia is one of the tallest tree which is a gymnosperm and it can be 130 - 140 metres tall.

The trees are generally pyramidal, with reddish-brown fibrous bark that is unusually fire resistant. The largest giant sequoia specimen is the General Sherman tree in Sequoia National Park.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is not true?
options: Tapetum helps in the dehiscence of anther
Exine of pollen grains is made up of sporopollenin
Pollen grains of many species cause severe allergies
Stored pollen in liquid nitrogen can be used in the crop breeding programmes
questions.solution: It is the final function of the anther that causes the release of pollen grains. A stomium is the opening in an anther usually between lip cells through which dehiscence occurs. Dehiscence of anther occurs due to stomium cells of endothecium

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Seed formation without fertilization in flowering plants involves the process of
questions.solution: Apomixis is a special mechanism to produce seeds without fertilization. Apomixis is an asexual mode of seed formation that produces clonal progeny with a maternal genotype. It primarily influences reproductive events in the ovule of the flower.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: Pollen grains of many species can germinate on the stigma of a flower, but only one pollen tube of the same species grows into the style.

Insects that consume pollen or nectar without bringing about pollination are called <math><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow></mrow></math> robbers.
Pollen germination and pollen tube growth are regulated by chemical components of pollen interacting with those of the pistil.
Some reptiles have also been reported as pollinators in some plant species.
questions.solution:
More than one pollen tube of the same species can grow into the style. It is frequently found in nature. 

Insects that consume pollen or nectar without bringing about pollination are called pollen/ nectar robbers. 

Pollen germination and pollen tube growth are regulated by chemical components of pollen interacting with those of the pistil. 

Some reptiles have also been reported as pollinators in some plant species.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Nomenclature is governed by certain universal rules. Which one of the following is contrary to the rules of nomenclature?
options: Biological names can be written in any language
The first words in a biological name represents the genus name, and the second is a specific epithet
The names are written in Latin and are italicized
When written by hand, the names are to be underlined
questions.solution: According to the rules of ICBN and ICZN, the original names were taken from Latin languages. New names are now derived from Latin language and are written in italics. Each name is composed of two parts, the generic name and specific epithet.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Water vapour comes out from the plant leaf through the stomatal opening. Through the same stomatal opening, carbon dioxide diffuses into the plant during photosynthesis. Reason out the above statements using one of the following options:

questions.q: Blood pressure in the pulmonary artery is:
options: Same as that in the aorta
More than that in the carotid
More than that in the pulmonary vein
Less than that in the venae cavae
questions.solution:
Blood pressure in different blood vessels:

Artery > Arteriole > Capillary > Venule > Vein (Vena cavae).

The pressure in arteries is more than that of pressure in veins as arteries receives blood directly from ventricles during ventricular systole. The wall of the arteries are thick and muscular. The flow of blood in arteries is fast as the blood in them is under great pressure.

The pressure in pulmonary aorta is more than that in the pulmonary vein as it receives blood directly from right ventricle during ventricular systole.

The pressure in pulmonary aorta is not same that of systemic aorta as pulmonary aorta supplies blood to lungs and systemic aorta supplies blood to the all the body parts.

Accumulation of fluid in the lung

Decrease in pH increases acidity of the blood that results in dissociation of oxygen and Hb which occurs in the body tissues.

questions.solution: AUG is a start codon that codes for methionine whereas UGA, UAA and UAG are stop codons. The Initiator codon is the first codon of a messenger RNA or mRNA transcript translated by a ribosome. questions.q: Analogous structures are a result of:
questions.solution: Analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution. Convergent evolution is the process whereby organisms not closely related (not monophyletic), independently evolve similar traits as a result of having to adapt to similar environments or ecological niches.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not a feature of the plasmids?
questions.solution:
Plasmids are extra chromosomal, double-stranded circular DNA.

They are used as vectors in genetic engineering.

In nature, plasmids provide one or more functional benefits to the host, such as resistance to antibiotics, degradative functions, and virulence.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The Taq polymerase enzyme is obtained from:
questions.solution:
The enzyme Taq polymerase is a thermostable enzyme that is obtained from Thermus aquaticus.

Taq DNA Polymerase catalyzes the incorporation of dNTPs into DNA during the polymerase chain reaction.

Taq polymerase helps in the replication of DNA. Due to the thermophilic nature, these enzymes are stable at high temperatures and used in PCR.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is a restriction endonuclease?
questions.solution:
Hind II is a type of restriction endonuclease.
A restriction enzyme or restriction endonuclease is an enzyme that cleaves DNA into fragments at or near specific recognition sites within the molecule known as restriction sites. Restrictions enzymes are one class of the broader endonuclease group of enzymes. Restriction enzymes are commonly classified into five types, which differ in their structure and whether they cut their DNA substrate at their recognition site, or if the recognition and cleavage sites are separate from one another. To cut DNA, all restriction enzymes make two incisions, once through each sugar-phosphate backbone (i.e. each strand) of the DNA double helix.
